item.title: The Explanation
item.content:encoded:
The idea was partially inspired by a synopsis of Jasper Fford's Lost in a Good Book. The idea was that the protagonist could read her way through different novels and could even take the other characters in those novels with her. I've since read the book. Not nearly as good as the first one, The Eyre Affair.

Anyhow, the synopsis immediately made me think of Fred. Why the heck can't Fred do that too? He should be able to, after all. He travels between books. Why can't he take others with him?

As I said, the original idea was based on him doing this, dragging a man from a post apocalyptic novel, Alas, Babylon, into the novelization of "The Monsters are Due on Maple Street." And then… well, let's be honest here. That idea sucks. You know what's awesome?

Fred dragging everyone he can out of every book he can get into to stop the Church of the Broken God from stealing SCP-882. THAT is a fucking awesome idea. And it played into the contest I was writing for at the time. So hell! That's what I did. Using the bookends, Fred saved the day! :D

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I have great amounts of love for SCP-423. The sheer range of available story (re)telling possibilities was only limited by the author's (and Fred's) choices of reading material. I always thought a vacation through John DeChancie's Castle Perilous series would be fun, but I don't trust my writing nearly enough to risk the dual injustice.

Troy, you have done justice to every piece you've touched on. I have no choice but to be boggled by the potential for collateral damage. I have one question: does the borrowed character only affect the copy as printed, or did you just invalidate LotR to save the world from the Church??

“For the glory of Gondor!” shouted the lead man, his sword held brazenly aloft.

Cardiforce instructed a sniper to shoot him.

+1. With a vengeance. For Gondor; and For Pony!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I stole the name and many of the original details from Alas, Babylon, then changed them as the story evolved. The original name (which I think is still in my sandbox) was "Alas, Maple Street, For Thy Judgment is Come", and was about Fred's adventures with Randy Bragg in Rodd Serling's "The Monsters are Due on Maple Street," the text version. It was fun, but it lacked any real kind of punch. If we ever do "SCP's Causing Mass Hysteria," I think it might be fun to revisit, but as of now, it's shelved.

Anyhow, I kept the name, because I liked it so much, and not much else.
